result.rationale: The diff's minimumTokenResponseSchema uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`, which evaluate to a fixed literal (e.g. '[object Object]'/'[ZodString]') as the property name, not a catch-all. So the schema requires a literal-number field under that bogus key and does not 'allow other properties' as the comment claims; safeParse will fail on any real token response (or, via zod strip, drop all other fields), making credential sync responses always invalid. Verifiable directly from the diff code.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` is defined with computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]`. These expressions evaluate immediately to a literal string (the Zod schema object's string representation), so the resulting Zod object schema only defines a property with that literal name, not “any string key”. This means the comment/intent (“assume any property with a number is the expiry” / “allow other properties”) is not implemented and the guard validates far less/differently than claimed. Correct approaches would be `z.record(...)` or `z.object({...}).catchall(...)`.
